intent: promote-to-pypi.yml: add bounded PyPI-CDN poll before post-publish smoke
notes: Fix v2.6.1 quick win #1 from the roadmap: recurring paper cut on Workflow C's `post-verify` job. PyPI's upload succeeds well before its CDN populates all edges — pip installs typically 404 for ~30-60s after a fresh publish. Every v2.5.2 → v2.6.0 promote failed the immediate post-publish smoke on this exact race (publish itself always succeeded; the failure was cosmetic-but-alarming).

Added a new `Wait for PyPI CDN to surface the new version` step to `post-verify`, sequenced BEFORE the existing install step. Polls `https://pypi.org/pypi/gator-command/${version}/json` (the JSON API endpoint the simple-index CDN reads from), bounded at **8 attempts × 15s = 120s max**. Typical warm-up is one or two attempts; the 120s ceiling catches genuine CDN incidents without hanging forever. On timeout, prints an explicit error message pointing the operator at `https://status.python.org/` and the publish job logs before manual re-run — no silent stall.

Alternative considered: straight `sleep 60`. Rejected — same worst-case wait as an unlucky poll but doesn't degrade gracefully when the CDN is faster (typical case wastes 30-45s), doesn't fail cleanly when the CDN is slower than expected (would silently 404 the install step), and doesn't distinguish "still warming" from "publish actually broken."

Charter: `.gator/charters/release-pipeline.md` — Workflow C `post-verify` step description updated to describe the new poll-before-install shape + link the historical incident context (v2.5.2 → v2.6.0 flakes).

Verification: cannot exercise the pipeline locally (workflow_dispatch requires PyPI publish credentials + `RELEASE_PIPELINE_ENABLED=true` gate). The new step is idiomatic bash + a stdlib `curl` invocation; no test infrastructure covers `.github/workflows/*.yml` in this repo. Real validation happens on the next release cycle — if the smoke passes in ≤8 attempts (~2 minutes total), the fix landed correctly.

Significance: minor. Fix scope is one workflow file + one charter update; the smoke behavior it fixes is cosmetic (publish succeeds, smoke fails post-publish, release notes get "known issue" boilerplate). But it's a recurring paper cut across 4 releases and the fix cost is trivial — worth cleaning up before the next release.
